reports.title: FRONTLINE PLC REPORTS RESULTS FOR THE THIRD QUARTER ENDED SEPTEMBER 30, 2026

desk.headline: Revenue more than doubled to $921.3m and adjusted EPS $2.38, beat; Q4 bookings at record rates, $2.38 dividend
results: Revenue rose to $921.3m from $432.7m a year ago, as tanker rates stayed very high with the Strait of Hormuz disrupted.
Adjusted profit was $530.9m ($2.38 a share), a little lower than Q2's $580.2m; reported profit of $641.4m includes a $111.2m gain on selling two ships.
Declared a $2.38 dividend for the quarter, after a special $0.80 paid in September from the ship sales.
Refinanced debt, cutting the average loan margin to 1.18% from 1.78% earlier in the year.

guidance.summary: No formal guidance, but Q4 bookings so far are the highest the company has recorded; it says full Q4 spot rates will come in below the booked rates because of empty return voyages.

points: Management described the market as without precedent; VLCC rates spiked near $1m a day outside Hormuz before easing.
It expects a record Q4 and a much higher floor for rates than in past cycles.
With 17 time charters ending from Q1 2027, it plans to lock in more fixed-rate charters.
Risks named: a large order book with fleet growth peaking in 2028, attacks on ships and possible sanctions changes.
